MACERATOR DESIGN FOR PORTIONED CHICKEN BREAST FOR FAST FOOD RESTAURANTS
SYSTEM FOR BULK HIGH PRESSURE PROCESSING AND RELATED METHOD
METHOD OF DETERMINING THE WEIGHT OF FOOD ITEMS

patents.source: USPTO Open Data Portal, granted patents since 2001, applicant phrase "jbt marel", 2026-10-06

reading.body:
JBT Marel's patent record is food-processing machinery, not AI infrastructure, so it does not sit on the compute supply chain this site tracks.

The sixteen granted patents since 2001 cover juice extraction, spiral conveyors, macerators, high-pressure processing, and food weighing. The most recent, granted 22 September 2026, claims a method to increase extraction capacity, power, and efficiency in a juice extraction machine. The company is classified under Special Industry Machinery, based in Chicago, and listed on the NYSE.

The word power appears in one patent title, and it refers to the mechanical throughput of a press rather than electrical supply. Nothing in the data connects this company to data centers, grid capacity, or AI compute. Its Illinois law exposure count of 375 is a general litigation or regulatory tally for the state, not an AI-specific figure.

What the data does not cover is decisive here. There are no products listed, no AI cases, and no model context protocol entries. The profile text is drawn from Wikipedia and describes a company spun off from FMC Technologies in 2008 with roots going back to 1884. A reader looking for a link between this registrant and AI scaling will not find one in these facts, and should not infer one from the presence of the word power in a patent title.

profile_text.body:
JBT Marel, formerly JBT Corporation and John Bean Technologies, makes food processing machinery and automated guided vehicles. It is based in Chicago, was incorporated in 2008 when FMC Technologies spun off its non-energy businesses, and traces its history to a company John Bean founded in 1884.

Source: Wikipedia, JBT Corporation, retrieved 22 September 2026.
